key_insight: A variational framework extends relativistic elasticity to include dissipative plastic deformation, with a relativistic yield criterion introduced through the second law of thermodynamics.
engineering_relevance: The framework provides a constitutive foundation for modeling permanent neutron-star crust deformation relevant to pulsar glitches, magnetar flares, and continuous gravitational-wave emission.
method: Adapt variational methods for dissipative fluids to relativistic elastic matter.
Incorporate plastic phenomenology with constitutive freedoms matching modern Newtonian theory.
Use the second law of thermodynamics to introduce a relativistic yield criterion.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical formulation but no numerical benchmarks, observational validation, or quantitative performance results.
watch_item: Numerical implementation and multiscale validation remain unestablished in the abstract, which focuses on the dissipative formulation.
